_comment: One entry per file or glob. `match` is an exact path or a glob (*, **, ?, {a,b}); a file takes the most specific entry that matches it. `summarize` folds a glob into one row (photos, videos). `virtual` entries are git-ignored local files that are never scanned. Every directory with files in it at the top level needs a line in `dirs`.

dirs.docs/: Guides for people, and the source of this overview.
dirs.docs/overview/: The overview's template, styles, script and authored text. Edit these, then run npm run build:overview.
dirs.docs/overview/catalog/: The authored half of the overview: descriptions, diagram, flows, API rows, variables, tests, troubleshooting.
dirs.media/: Photos and videos the pages use. Only these file types are served, from /media/.
dirs.pages/: The built pages (written by tools/build-site.js from the exports and site/patches/; do not edit by hand) and the Coming soon page, which is written by hand.
dirs.pages_original/: Untouched exports from Claude Design. The build starts from these, never from pages/.
dirs.server/config/: Reading .env and the real environment into one settings object.
dirs.server/lib/: The site map, errors, logging, and the loader for the Design Studio.
dirs.server/middleware/: The guards every request passes through, and the response headers.
dirs.server/routes/: One module per group of routes: pages (and the Coming soon page), media, API, docs, studio.
dirs.site/: The site as data: site.json, shared HTML components and the JSON patches that turn exports into pages.
dirs.site/patches/: One JSON patch file per page (anchored edits, applied by the build).
dirs.site/patches/snippets/: Code the patches insert into the pages.
dirs.tests/: Automated checks: node:test, shared helpers, a dev stack on throw-away settings, browser tests.
dirs.tests/js/: node:test suites for the server, the site build and the overview. Run: npm run test:js
dirs.tests/helpers/: Small helpers shared by the server tests.
dirs.tests/dev/: A runnable dev stack: the real site with the Design Studio mounted, against mock GPU services and no database, for trying the whole flow without credentials.
dirs.tests/e2e/: Browser tests that drive Chrome through the real pages and the studio's start-up. Run: npm run test:e2e
dirs.tools/: Scripts that build, check and run things. The site works without them.
dirs.swatchroom/: The Design Studio (Swatchroom 5), copied in unchanged: its Express routes and libraries, the browser code, the Python scan models, the Modal GPU blueprint, and its own tests and guides. The website mounts it; start with swatchroom/README.md.
dirs.server/auth/: Sign-in: accounts, one-time codes, sessions, Google, the firm look-up, the CRM queue, and the settings the admin panel will manage.
dirs.server/auth/providers/: How a one-time code leaves the server: SMTP, Twilio, a webhook for any SMS gateway.
dirs.python/: The website's own Python environment (python/.venv, not committed): gallery-dl, run as a separate program by the inspiration import. Not the Design Studio's (swatchroom/python/).
dirs.site/inspiration/: The browser side of the inspiration import (target C3): the paste question, the crop screen, the hand-over to the Design Studio, and the one list of sites it reads. Served from /inspiration/assets/ by a fixed list of names.
dirs.server/lib/inspiration/: The server side of the inspiration import: safe fetching of an address a visitor chose, gallery-dl, picture checks, tokens and limits.
dirs.server/catalogue/: The website's catalogue gateway (targets C3, C4, C5, C7, D1): client and admin routes, the Modal client, the GCS signer, validation and settings. Mints signed URLs and forwards small requests; never does model work itself. See catalogue/ARCHITECTURE.md section 7.
dirs.site/catalogue-ui/: The browser side of the Finder page and the catalogue admin screen (targets C3, C4, C5, C7, D1): client.js (the shared API client, camera and photo-resize helpers), finder.js, admin.js, catalogue-ui.css. Served from /catalogue-ui/assets/ by a fixed list of names (server/routes/catalogueUi.js), the same pattern as site/inspiration/.
dirs.catalogue/: The real-catalogue retrieval engine (Python), ported from terucon-cat-1.ipynb: extraction, encoders, the Vertex/Gemini captions, the publisher (MongoDB + GCS + a Modal cache), the search service and the Modal app. Not shipped in the website's Docker image. Start with catalogue/ARCHITECTURE.md.

Code the home and studio patches insert: asks the website to wake the studio's GPU services as soon as the page opens (at most once a minute per tab).

POST /api/studio/warmup on its own: the on/off switch, the count-only answer, no studio mounted.

The path through the site: the studio page comes from the swatchroom's export, the wake-up is on the landing and studio pages only, the hero link, the Coming soon page, every page reachable from the landing page.

The studio on its own (node server/index.js) against the studio mounted in the website, same requests: status, headers and body must match for its files, its session, its passcode refusals, its wake-up and a raw photo upload. The behavioural proof that mounting changed nothing.
A GPU service that answers /healthz with 401 is not shown as warm, the failure is logged, and the next visit retries only that service.

What git commits and Docker copies, from the outside: nothing in swatchroom/ is ignored except its secrets and caches (an unanchored models/ rule once hid its Mongoose models), secrets are ignored, and the image leaves them out.

In front of the studio's API when its passcode is off: each browser (an HttpOnly cookie) can only list, open and delete rooms it made; the costly routes (Gemini, scans, room analysis, room saves) are rate limited per browser and per address.
Who made each saved room: a separate MongoDB collection (room_owners) made through the studio's own connection. The studio's rooms and files are never changed.
A small sliding-window counter (per key, per hour) used by the studio shield; in memory.
GET /api/analytics: the PostHog key and host for the pages (the website's POSTHOG_KEY, else the studio's), or {enabled: false}.

Code every page patch inserts (the Coming soon page carries a copy): loads PostHog, records page views, clicks and forms, masks all text and blocks photos in session replay, and leaves Do Not Track browsers alone.
The studio shield with an in-memory room store: rooms are private per browser, the limits and their messages, nothing else is touched.
/api/analytics, its key and host rules, the localhost rule, and that every page carries the one snippet and no key.
The website with the studio mounted and the passcode off: the studio's own passcode setting is ignored, the owner cookie, the anti-framing headers and the limits.

The sign-in page, written by hand. One box for an e-mail or mobile number, the code, the sign-up form (firm suggested from a business e-mail), Google One Tap. Served at /login with its own strict Content-Security-Policy.
The account page, written by hand: edit details, confirm or change e-mail / number with a code, sign out, delete the account. Served at /account, members only.

Code every page patch inserts: the header link says Sign in or Account, and an API answer of "please sign in" leads to the sign-in page. No camelCase name before an = (the pages' runtime rewrites those).
Puts sign-in together and decides whether it is safe to run (fails closed, says why): sessions and cookies, the gate for pages and for the studio's costly API, the admin token.
What sign-in reads from .env. Secrets are kept in settings.authSecrets, which does not show up when settings are listed, logged or sent.

Every setting the admin panel will manage (rate limits, code rules, sessions, open ways in, SMS countries, firm look-up, Zoho field names) with its type, default and hard bounds. Stored in the database as the difference from the defaults.
E-mail, mobile number, name and firm: strict normalisation, the mailbox key limits are counted by (plus-tags, Gmail dots), the firm name guessed from a domain.

One-time codes: asking for one (same answer for members and strangers, wait between codes, caps per address, per network and per day) and using one (five tries counted atomically, spent once, locks across codes).
Accounts. Only a verified e-mail, phone or Google id signs anybody in, each at most one account; what a person merely typed is an unproved claim and never a way in.
Sessions: a random token in the cookie, only its hash in the database, ended by idle time, age, sign-out, sign-out everywhere or deleting the account.
Checks Google's ID token with node:crypto: RS256 only, Google's keys by kid, issuer, audience, expiry, verified e-mail and the one-use nonce.

A firm name for a business e-mail: from the domain, or from the firm's website, read with SSRF protection (public addresses only, checked as the connection is made; https, same domain, size and time limits).

Zoho CRM: the API client (token kept and refreshed once, upsert by e-mail, update, delete), the record builder with the admin's field names, and the retry queue that holds sign-ups until Zoho is connected.
Counting for limits: in memory per network address (IPv6 per /64) and in the database per address or number and for the whole site.
The security log (90 days): what happened, never a code, a token or a full address.
Where accounts live: the studio's MongoDB connection (collections terucon_*) or memory, behind one calling surface, with the unique indexes that make one verified address one account.
A strict in-memory stand-in for the part of MongoDB's collection API the sign-in uses, so the same code runs in tests and without a database.
Random tokens, hashes, keyed hashes and constant-time comparison: the only place sign-in touches cryptography.
Chooses the e-mail and SMS senders from .env; one that is not set up properly is not offered, and says what is wrong.
A small SMTP client: TLS or STARTTLS with certificate checks, no unencrypted login to a remote host, nothing a visitor typed can become a header.
The words of the code messages: fixed text plus digits, no links.
The sign-in API: /api/auth/* (start, verify, Google, profile, firm hint, contact confirmation, logout, delete).
The sign-in admin API: /api/auth/admin/* (settings, events, status, unlock, CRM queue), behind AUTH_ADMIN_TOKEN.
Builds a Content-Security-Policy from a hand-written page (its inline script and style by hash).
Only one spelling of /api reaches anything: /API/rooms and the like are 404 (they used to slide past every protection into the studio).
The sign-in services on the in-memory store with a movable clock and senders that keep the codes.
Signs a test visitor in through the real endpoints, so tests walk through the gate instead of switching it off.
E-mail, phone, name and firm normalisation and the firm-from-domain guess.
The database calls sign-in needs, checked on the in-memory store and, with AUTH_TEST_MONGODB_URI set, on a real MongoDB.
One-time codes, sessions, accounts and settings: limits, locks, races, expiry, purposes, pre-account takeover.
The sign-in API as a browser uses it: sign up, sign in again, cookies, sign out, contacts, deletion, Google through the real verifier, and fail-closed.
Every page but the landing page is for members, whatever way the address is written; the policy of the hand-written pages.
The admin API: off without a token, brute-force limit, settings with bounds, events, unlock, CRM controls.
The SMTP client against a pretend mail server (TLS, STARTTLS, injection), Twilio, the webhook, and reading .env.
Google's token: forgeries (alg none, HS256 with the public key, wrong key, tampered), audience, issuer, expiry, nonce, key rotation.
The firm look-up and its SSRF defences: private, loopback and metadata addresses, DNS rebinding, redirects, size and time limits.
Zoho: token handling, the record, the queue (retry, backoff, credentials arriving later, deletion), against a pretend Zoho.
The security pass, kept as tests: every attack that was sent to the running server (case-variant /API paths, brute force, races, CSRF, NoSQL, prototype pollution, SSRF, enumeration, takeover ...).

The Inspiration page, written by hand: a box for a link with Paste and Import buttons, upload and drag-and-drop, the sites it reads, recent imports. Served at /inspiration, members only, under a strict Content-Security-Policy (`strict+images`). No inline script or style attribute.
